title: Best Keyhole Alternatives for Real-Time Hashtag Tracking in 2026
summary: Keyhole's pricing page now redirects straight to Muck Rack's demo funnel — there's no way to buy just Keyhole anymore. Compare 5 real alternatives for 2026.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Keyhole's brand, domain, and legacy marketing pages are still live in 2026, but every purchase path — pricing, plan options, even the old free-trial signup link — now 301-redirects to a gated Muck Rack demo-request form. There's no way to buy "just Keyhole" anymore, at any price, through any page on keyhole.co. Muck Rack owns the actual underlying technology but has reframed it for PR teams with real caps (Instagram hashtag-only, TikTok limited to 90 posts per 6-hour refresh). For teams that specifically want Keyhole's original real-time hashtag-campaign use case, Hootsuite's newer TikTok Hashtag Monitoring feature is the closest genuine replacement, while Brand24, Awario, and Determ cover budget keyword/hashtag tracking with varying TikTok gaps.


If you've bookmarked keyhole.co from an old campaign report or a "best hashtag tracking tools" roundup, you might still expect a pricing page and a free trial button. That expectation is outdated. Every third-party comparison still floating around citing "$179/month" is describing a price that no longer exists anywhere on Keyhole's own site.


Get this wrong and you'll spend an afternoon clicking "Start Free Trial" buttons that all funnel into the same place: a lead-gen form for a different company entirely. This piece covers whether Keyhole is still purchasable in 2026, what it was actually good at before the acquisition, what happened to its technology afterward, and which alternative actually fits a team that just wants real-time hashtag and campaign tracking.


## Is Keyhole Still a Standalone Product You Can Buy in 2026?


No — not through any self-serve path. Keyhole's homepage still resolves as its own branded page, with a headline reading "Keyhole's Social Listening is available on Muck Rack," but the only two calls to action are "Book a Demo" and "Explore Muck Rack." There's no pricing or signup button anywhere on it (Source:[Keyhole homepage, live fetch Aug 2026](https://keyhole.co/) ).


**Zombie brand** : a company's original name, domain, and marketing pages remain live and indexed, but every functional purchase or signup path has been redirected to the acquiring company's own funnel. That's precisely Keyhole's current state.` keyhole.co/pricing` ,` keyhole.co/plan-options` , and even the legacy free-trial URL` keyhole.co/register-product/20` all 301-redirect to a Muck Rack landing page titled "Keyhole + Muck Rack," whose copy reads: "You're in the right place! Muck Rack acquired Keyhole." The form on that page collects a business email, name, company, and job title — and submits to "Request Demo," not a checkout (confirmed via three independent redirect tests, live fetch Aug 2026).


Legacy content pages are still indexed too — a page titled "Twitter Hashtag Analytics | Real-Time Hashtag Tracking For Twitter" still displays a "Start Free Trial" button, but that button routes to` /plan-options` , which redirects to the same Muck Rack gate. Even the site's own footer legal links — About, Privacy Policy, Terms of Service — now resolve to` muckrack.com` domains, not Keyhole's own. Existing customers can still log in at` keyhole.co/users/login` , and that page even offers a "Login via MuckRack.com" option, evidence of backend account merging — but there's no new-account signup link anywhere on it. An independent third-party comparison confirms the same shift from the outside: "Keyhole is now part of Muck Rack's social listening platform. The buying motion may feel more 'demo and quote' than self-serve for many teams" (Source:[FindMeCreators — Best Keyhole Alternatives for 2026](https://www.findmecreators.com/blog/keyhole-alternatives) ).


This is a distinct pattern from other acquisitions in this space. Digimind fully renamed into Onclusive Social — the brand disappeared entirely. Keyhole keeps its name, domain, and login portal, but its actual buying process has been completely replaced. Third-party pricing aggregators still publish "$179/month (Professional, 3 trackers)" as if it's a live, purchasable figure (Source:[Socialrails — Keyhole Review 2026](https://socialrails.com/blog/keyhole-review) ) — that number is a pre-redirect historical reference, not something you can actually pay today.


## What Was Keyhole Actually Good at for Hashtag and Campaign Tracking?


Real-time hashtag and campaign tracking was Keyhole's entire identity. The product centered on live, shareable dashboards built for event hashtags, influencer campaign measurement, and conference or activation tracking — the kind of thing a marketing team pulls up mid-event to watch numbers move. Named customer proof still displayed on the site places it squarely in that live-event space: WWF's "We Love Cities" campaign across 50 locations, Billboard's Hot 100 Festival brand monitoring, and NBC Sports' American Century Golf Championship tracking (Source:[Keyhole homepage, live fetch Aug 2026](https://keyhole.co/) ).


Keyhole holds a solid 4.3 out of 5 aggregate rating on G2 from roughly 70 reviews — respectable, though a noticeably smaller review base than category peers. Muck Rack itself, by comparison, carries 433 reviews at 4.5/5 (Source:[G2 — Keyhole Reviews, 2026](https://www.g2.com/products/keyhole/reviews) ;[G2 — Muck Rack Reviews, 2026](https://www.g2.com/products/muck-rack/reviews) ). Even at its peak, though, the product had a structural ceiling: it was analytics and tracking only, with no scheduling or publishing layer, and its video capability topped out at YouTube analytics — there was never a confirmed TikTok-native video or audio analysis feature, even before the acquisition.


## What Happened to Keyhole's Technology After the Muck Rack Acquisition?


Muck Rack acquired Keyhole in September 2024 and shipped the integration as "Muck Rack Social Listening" in February 2025 (Source:[Muck Rack Blog, Sept 3, 2024](https://muckrack.com/blog/2024/09/03/muckrack-acquires-keyhole/) ;[Muck Rack Blog, Feb 12, 2025](https://muckrack.com/blog/2025/02/12/introducing-integrated-social-listening) ). Keyhole's own blog post at the time, titled "Big News: Keyhole Is Now Part Of Muck Rack!", framed it as continuity for existing users while folding the roadmap into Muck Rack's PR-first product.


The resulting product is real, but meaningfully capped compared to what a dedicated hashtag-campaign tool typically offers. Instagram tracking is hashtag-only — there's no general keyword search — and it's limited to 30 search terms plus 30 hashtags per connected account on a rolling 7-day window. TikTok tracking is capped at 90 posts per refresh, checked every 6 hours (Source:[Muck Rack Help Center — Tracking Hashtags and Keywords on Instagram](https://help.muckrack.com/en/articles/11096178-tracking-hashtags-and-keywords-on-instagram) ;[Muck Rack Help Center — Platforms Tracked](https://help.muckrack.com/en/articles/11096145-social-listening-platforms-tracked-by-muck-rack) ). Muck Rack's own 2026 product investment — Media List Agent, Curation Engine, Boolean Builder, Generative Pulse — is entirely PR-workflow AI; none of it deepens the social listening side further.

Hootsuite is the standout on this list for anyone specifically replacing Keyhole's hashtag-campaign use case: its TikTok Hashtag Monitoring feature, live since May 2026, tracks up to 50 brand hashtags per token, with a backfill of up to 1,000 top-performing posts from the prior 90 days so a new connection isn't starting from zero — built on the official TikTok mentions API and explicitly positioned for campaign measurement and trend research (Source:[Hootsuite — TikTok Hashtag Monitoring](https://www.hootsuite.com/whats-new/tiktok-hashtag-monitoring) ;[Hootsuite Blog, May 2026](https://blog.hootsuite.com/new-features-may-2026/) ). It lives inside a broader scheduling and publishing suite rather than a standalone tracker, and the deepest listening tier (Talkwalker's 150M-source coverage) is Enterprise-gated, but it's a genuine, real-time, hashtag-specific capability — closer to what Keyhole originally did than anything else on this list.


Awario and Determ are both a harder trade for a team leaving Keyhole specifically for hashtag campaigns: neither covers TikTok at any tier, which is a gap Keyhole itself never had. Brand24 sits in between — cheaper than Keyhole's old pricing and keyword/hashtag-first, but its brand-mention matching is text-only, with no video or audio understanding of what's actually said or shown on screen.


## Which Keyhole Alternative Fits Your Team's Hashtag-Tracking Needs?


It splits by what you actually need the tool to see. A team that wants the closest thing to Keyhole's original real-time hashtag-campaign dashboard — including genuine TikTok coverage — should look at[Hootsuite](https://syncly.app/blog/hootsuite-alternatives) first; its dedicated hashtag-monitoring feature is the nearest functional match on this list. A team that's fine with Muck Rack's PR-oriented framing and doesn't mind Instagram's hashtag-only limits can simply follow the acquisition and adopt Muck Rack directly, since it owns Keyhole's original technology outright. Teams prioritizing budget over TikTok coverage should look at[Brand24](https://syncly.app/blog/8-best-brand24-alternatives-for-teams-ready-to-cover-video-too) for keyword/hashtag tracking, or[Awario](https://syncly.app/blog/awario-alternatives-for-8-tools-compared-on-tiktok-coverage-pricing-and-reviews) specifically if Boolean search precision matters more than any video platform at all.[Determ](https://syncly.app/blog/determ-alternatives-for-10-tools-compared-on-pricing-and-video-coverage) fits teams whose monitoring need is PR/news-first rather than hashtag-campaign-first.


None of these tools closes the gap Keyhole never actually had, though: catching brand and product mentions inside video content that was never tagged with a hashtag at all.[Syncly Social](https://syncly.app/) isn't a hashtag-campaign dashboard and shouldn't be positioned as one — it has no live event leaderboards, no influencer-campaign hashtag exports, none of Keyhole's original shareable-report format. What it does specifically is catch[untagged, spoken, and visual brand mentions](https://syncly.app/social/feature/video-analysis) inside TikTok, Reels, and Shorts content that fires only when a hashtag or keyword is actually typed — the exact ceiling every hashtag-tracking tool structurally hits — through[social listening](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) and[competitor analysis](https://syncly.app/social/solution/competitor-analysis) built for video content specifically. A brand running a hashtag campaign would pair Syncly Social with whichever hashtag tracker fits above, not replace one with the other.


## Key Takeaways


-


Keyhole's brand, domain, legacy marketing pages, and existing-customer login all remain live in 2026 — but every purchase or signup path now redirects to a gated Muck Rack demo-request form. There's no way to buy "just Keyhole" anymore, at any price.


-


Third-party pricing aggregators still cite a "$179/month" figure as if it's live and purchasable — it's a pre-redirect historical reference, not a current buyable price on keyhole.co.


-


Muck Rack acquired Keyhole in September 2024 and owns its actual underlying technology, but caps it meaningfully: Instagram tracking is hashtag-only (30 terms + 30 hashtags/account, 7-day window), and TikTok is capped at 90 posts per 6-hour refresh.


-


Hootsuite's TikTok Hashtag Monitoring feature, live since May 2026, is the closest genuine replacement for Keyhole's original real-time hashtag-campaign use case, including actual TikTok coverage and a 1,000-post/90-day backfill.


-


Awario and Determ cover zero TikTok at any tier — a harder gap than Keyhole itself ever had — making them a weaker fit specifically for teams leaving Keyhole over hashtag campaigns centered on short-form video.


## The Verdict


Keyhole isn't gone, exactly — it's a maintained-for-existing-users brand with no door open for anyone new. If your team's job is genuinely real-time hashtag and campaign tracking with TikTok in the mix, Hootsuite's dedicated hashtag-monitoring feature is the nearest functional replacement available today. If PR workflow matters more than campaign dashboards, Muck Rack already owns what Keyhole used to be. Either way, don't let a stale "$179/month" citation from an old comparison post send you chasing a signup page that hasn't existed for over a year.
